A saving throw, also called a save, represents an attempt to resist a spell, a trap, a poison, a disease, or a similar threat. You don't normally decide to make a saving throw; you are forced to make one because your character or monster is at risk of harm. To make a saving throw, roll a d20 and add the appropriate ability modifier. For example, you use your Dexterity modifier for a Dexterity saving throw. A saving throw can be modified by a situational bonus or penalty and can be affected by advantage and disadvantage, as determined by the Director. Each class gives proficiency in at least two saving throws. The wizard, for example, is proficient in Intelligence saves. As with skill proficiencies, proficiency in a saving throw lets a character add his or her proficiency bonus to saving throws made using a particular ability score. Some monsters have saving throw proficiencies as well. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw is determined by the effect that causes it. For example, the DC for a saving throw allowed by a spell is determined by the caster's spellcasting ability and proficiency bonus. The result of a successful or failed saving throw is also detailed in the effect that allows the save. Usually, a successful save means that a creature suffers no harm, or reduced harm, from an effect.

traits.text: At the start of your turn, you regain hit points equal to your proficiency bonus if you have at least 1 hit point. If you take acid or fire damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.text: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

traits.name: Claws
traits.text: Your claws are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal slashing damage equal to 1d4 + your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: You can speak, read, and write Common and Giant.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.text: Your Wisdom score increases by 1.

traits.name: Toxic Secretions
traits.text: When a creature hits you with a melee attack while within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to deal poison damage to the attacker equal to your proficiency bonus. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

traits.name: Disease Immunity
traits.text: You are immune to disease.

traits.name: Swamp Camouflage
traits.text: You have proficiency in the Stealth skill. When you attempt to hide in a swamp or marsh environment, you can do so even when only lightly obscured.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.text: Your Strength score increases by 1 (for a total of +2 to Strength).

traits.name: Stone Hide
traits.text: Your AC increases by 1.

traits.name: Earth Affinity
traits.text: You have advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made against effects that would knock you prone.

traits.name: One with Stone
traits.text: You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in rocky terrain.

traits.name: Ability Score Increase
traits.text: Your Charisma score increases by 1.

traits.name: Enhanced Regeneration
traits.text: When you use your Regeneration trait, you regain additional hit points equal to your Constitution modifier.

traits.name: Blood Magic
traits.text: You know the blood manipulation cantrip. When you reach 3rd level, you can cast the false life spell once per day. When you reach 5th level, you can also cast the vampiric touch spell once per day. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

traits.name: Vitality Transfer
traits.text: As an action, you can touch a willing creature and transfer some of your life force to them. You take damage equal to your level, and the target regains hit points equal to twice that amount. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

operational.targets: Choose the mode determined by your casting class's preserved school/rank: Divination rank 0 targets one perceived object or creature within 30 feet; Abjuration rank 1 surveys the area within 30 feet of you. Both require line of effect.
operational.resolution: Automatic after legal casting; Abjuration mode additionally requires your ordinary class casting focus F.
operational.effect: Divination rank 0: learn only whether the selected creature or object currently contains or is affected by an explicit poison record. Abjuration rank 1: learn whether such poison is present and its actual source-authorized type, name or category records. This area report does not identify which creature or object carries which poison or give their location.
operational.scaling: None. Casting through another class requires that class's own actual repertoire and level access; paying extra RP never changes the mode.
operational.limitations: Uses existing mechanical poison records; it cannot invent a poison, hidden creature taxonomy or diagnosis from theme. Does not identify disease, Corruption, curses or the cause of unrelated symptoms, prescribe an antidote, reveal statistics, cure anything, or look through total cover. Where no precise poison type is source-defined, Abjuration reports unknown poison rather than inventing a formula or secret identity. Known/prepared access, class-level gates, legal components, line of effect, payment before resolution, concentration transitions, Dissonance, Refrain and class cadence follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. No automatic scaling or generic upcast. A generic Poisoned condition qualifies only if its actual provenance is poison-linked. Neither mode reports dose, save DC, severity, onset, duration, cure or unrelated medical conditions. Divination never reports poison type or identity; ordinary deductions from an authorized result remain possible.

# Hush-Broker Plaguehand

**Family:** Hush-Broker
**Knowledge status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports
**Publication classification:** Licensed expedition reference
**Dungeon range:** T3-T5, Floors 21-50
**Primary source:** Contraband contracts, Pact Court testimony, and interdicted ledgers
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below
**Encounter role:** Striker

## What It Is

Hush-Broker Plaguehand manufactures quarantine and offers costly relief. It prefers controlled panic to open slaughter, because a frightened survivor can sign, testify, carry debt, or lead the Broker to a more valuable target.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Blank spaces in ledgers; bells wrapped in cloth; witnesses who repeat the same sentence word for word; quarantine marks that do not match local practice; doors that open only after someone states a name. Nearby insects die before larger animals show symptoms.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Religion** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 12 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 16 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 20 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Professional Record with Deep Reports  
**Primary source:** Contraband contracts, Pact Court testimony, and interdicted ledgers  
**Reliability:** High through Floor 30; moderate below  
**Last confirmed:** Current upper-range reports; older deep reports  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 21-30  
**Rumored range:** Floors 31-50

### Unsettling Evidence

Recovered contracts use the words petition, prisoner, and fulfillment in mutually contradictory ways. Goblin copies are the oldest surviving versions and differ by only one or two words per generation. The field record preserves the contradiction but does not present a hidden cosmology as established fact.

### Deep-Record Warning

Exact numbers and tactics below reflect the best reconstruction available to licensed expeditions. The Director may vary phases, recharge signs, or retreat behavior to reflect incomplete in-world knowledge and changes between Openings.

## Stat Block

**Medium Fiend, Lawful Evil**  
**Challenge** 7 (2900 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T3-T5 · **Floors** 21-50
**Armor** 15 · **Hit Points** 246 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 13 (+1) | 14 (+2) | 15 (+2) | 14 (+2) | 13 (+1) | 16 (+3) |

**Resistances** fire, necrotic  
**Immunities** None  
**Condition Immunities** frightened  
**Tactical Vulnerability** destroyed or invalidated contract seals  
**Save DC** 14  

### Traits

**Contract-Bound.** A visible seal or written clause empowers one of its attacks; destroying or invalidating it suppresses that feature until the end of the next round.

### Actions

**Multiattack.** The creature makes 3 attacks using the actions below.

**Contagion Touch.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+8 necrotic damage (average 17).

**Quarantine Brand.** *Attack:* +7 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 2d8+7 poison damage (average 16).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Contagion Touch** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses **Quarantine Brand** to punish anyone who tries to stabilize that target. It keeps a witness, hostage, or written object between itself and the Expedition and withdraws into jurisdiction rather than dying for pride.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for necrotic, poison damage.
- Carry blank witness cards and refuse unexamined aid.

**Combat Priority**

Destroy or isolate the seal-bearing implement, then pressure the Broker away from witnesses.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **destroyed or invalidated contract seals**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when its full multiattack reaches the support line. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Broker sites are legal terrain as much as physical terrain. Seals, witness circles, sample cabinets, toll chains, and written names can become hazards. Destroying the room may activate clauses rather than end them.

Hush-Brokers are fiendish intermediaries who convert fear, silence, quarantine, and contract language into enforceable power. They prefer an Expedition that survives indebted to them over one that dies free.

They bargain sincerely inside the exact wording they offer. Precision protects an Expedition better than moral outrage.

## Treasure and Harvest

**Harvest skill:** Religion · **Harvest DC:** 14 · **Base time:** 2 hours  

| Component | Tier | Drop / Value |
|---|---:|---|
| contract ash | 2 | Director-set |
| hush-salt | 2 | Director-set |
| court seal | 2 | Director-set |

Broker remains contain contract ash, hush-salt, branded vellum, black bile, and court seals. Unlicensed possession can be treated as proof of a stolen debt.

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change the contract object, emergency being exploited, and enforcement role. A weaker Broker with a stronger legal position can be more dangerous than an elite combatant.

# Order-Drone Tetrad

**Family:** Order Drone
**Knowledge status:** Established Field Record
**Publication classification:** Public
**Dungeon range:** T1, Floors 1-10
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies
**Reliability:** High
**Encounter role:** Predator or pressure creature

## What It Is

Order-Drone Tetrad is a distributed containment intelligence. Its bodies are dangerous individually, but the real weapon is the geometry they maintain between one another and the terrain.

## What Experienced Expeditions Notice

Evenly spaced scoring on stone; dust cleared in repeated arcs; metallic clicks answering one another around corners; corpses moved out of pathways rather than looted. Loose metal turns to face the same direction.

## Creature Knowledge

Use **Engineering or Arcana** unless the Director approves a more specific approach.

| Result | Information Learned |
|---|---|
| DC 11 | Creature family, usual habitat, and dominant attack type. |
| DC 15 | The first reliable counter and the sign that its strongest ability is ready. |
| DC 19 | Its defining tactical weakness, safe harvest method, and likely retreat condition. |

## Knowledge Status and Reliability

**Status:** Established Field Record  
**Primary source:** Sentinel maintenance records and battlefield salvage studies  
**Reliability:** High  
**Last confirmed:** Current Opening and prior guild registries  
**Confirmed range:** Floors 1-10  
**Rumored range:** Regional variants may extend beyond the confirmed range

## Stat Block

**Small Construct, Chaotic Good**  
**Challenge** 1/4 (50 XP budget) · **Dungeon Range** T1 · **Floors** 1-10
**Armor** 11 · **Hit Points** 18 · **Speed** 40 ft.

| STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 9 (-1) | 16 (+3) | 16 (+3) | 8 (-1) | 10 (+0) | 6 (-2) |

**Resistances** poison, psychic  
**Immunities** disease  
**Condition Immunities** charmed, exhaustion, poisoned  
**Tactical Vulnerability** forced movement that breaks formation  
**Save DC** 13  

### Traits

**Formation Intelligence.** While within 20 feet of another body in its unit, it gains +1 Armor and cannot be surprised.

### Actions

**Iron Slam.** *Attack:* +3 to hit, one target. *Hit:* 1d6+1 bludgeoning damage (average 4).

## How It Fights

It opens with **Iron Slam** against the target most capable of controlling its movement. It uses every action to preserve formation and converts broken lines into immediate repositioning.

## How to Defeat It

**Prepare Before Contact**

- Prepare resistance or mitigation for bludgeoning damage.
- Bring forced movement and terrain creation.

**Combat Priority**

Split the formation and destroy the coordinating body.

**Exploit**

The defining weakness is **forced movement that breaks formation**. Treat this as an encounter solution rather than an automatic damage vulnerability. Successful Research, Recon, or Resource actions should make the exploit easier or safer.

**Withdraw When**

Withdraw or change the objective when the creature reaches favorable terrain or isolates a target. A failed retreat against this creature usually costs more than abandoning the immediate treasure.

## Habitat, Goals, and Lair

Drone zones favor grids, choke points, rotating doors, magnetic floors, and lines that improve formation attacks. Their positions are part of the stat block.

Order-Drones are collective constructs designed to solve movement, trespass, and containment problems through formation. A “pair,” “tetrad,” or “quintet” is one tactical intelligence distributed across several bodies.

Correct credentials, maintenance codes, or a higher-priority emergency may redirect them. Emotional appeals do nothing unless the automaton was built to interpret them.

**Harvest skill:** Engineering · **Harvest DC:** 11 · **Base time:** 20 minutes

## Variants and Encounter Use

Change formation size, command priority, and terrain. Each added body should expand tactical geometry rather than simply add attacks.

## Petrified

**Preserved Core text:** Incapacitated stone-like state; resistance to damage, immunity to poison/disease, weight ×10.

**Effect:** The creature becomes an inanimate stone-like substance, weight ×10, ceases aging, is Incapacitated, cannot move or speak, is unaware, automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves, and attacks against it have advantage. It has resistance to all damage except Corruption damage, and immunity to poison and disease; existing poison/disease effects are suspended rather than removed.

**Application:** Only an effect explicitly inflicting Petrified applies it.

**Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/removal rule. Suspended poison/disease resumes if Petrified ends and the underlying effect has not otherwise expired or been cured.

**Stacking:** Does not stack.

**Immunities and specific exceptions:** Petrification immunity blocks application. Corruption resistance is not granted because the special Core Corruption rule requires explicit Corruption protection.

**Compatible V6/source details:**

- V6: transformed into inanimate substance, weight ×10, cease aging, Incapacitated, cannot move/speak, unaware, attacks against have advantage, automatically fails Strength/Dexterity saves, resistance to all damage, immunity to poison and disease, existing poison/disease suspended rather than neutralized.

**Source conflicts:**

## Administration and uninterrupted application

An oral antidote or hazard buff takes **one Action and one available hand** to drink or feed to one willing or Incapacitated active creature within 5 feet. It needs a physically compatible ingestion route; inability to swallow blocks oral use. No forced dose to an unwilling active creature, no inhaled attack, coating or later tea-brewing Action is implied. “Active” here means not Dead; a still-dying creature can receive a compatible dose. Creature type alone does not prohibit a compatible route, and an actual source-specific healing restriction still controls.

A balm, compress, healing salve or poultice takes **one uninterrupted active minute**, with one available hand and continuing touch/access to compatible tissue. The recipient must be willing or Incapacitated. In initiative, the applier spends an Action on each of **10 consecutive regular turns**, and at least 60 elapsed seconds must pass. Extra Actions or inserted turns cannot shorten the interval. Track elapsed start time as well as the Action count; finish only when both requirements are met. Resolution occurs at the first moment both the required regular-turn Action count and the elapsed-time minimum are satisfied; no eleventh Action, or one-hundred-first Action for Panacea, is required. If the final required Action occurs before the elapsed minimum, the application remains continuously in progress until that elapsed deadline and resolves then, provided all required hand, touch/access and recipient eligibility have remained uninterrupted. One applier completes the whole application; workers cannot divide, parallelize or hand off those Actions. An active recipient may perform other legal activity if it keeps the necessary access; no new immobilization is imposed.

Choose and lock the actual recipient when beginning. Spend one dose at legal start. Before-start illegality prevents starting and spending; an interruption after start loses the paid dose with no result. Loss of required access, missing a required Action, applier incapacity or the recipient becoming ineligible interrupts. Taking damage alone is not an interruption and prompts no invented concentration check. The recipe grants no HP, condition removal or stabilization before completion; all ordinary dying clocks continue. A healer's kit may be needed first to keep a patient alive during the minute.

The applier is working and cannot claim that active time as rest. A recipient may receive care while resting only if the actual rest procedure permits it. A remedy does not pay the separate medical-kit, Supply or time costs of a different treatment project. Administering it is not a crafting check and grants no manufacturing XP.

## Antidotes

On resolution, **end all currently present removable applications of Poisoned**, then grant advantage on saving throws against poison for the card's printed duration. Source-specific applications that expressly cannot be removed this way remain. Ending Poisoned does not itself end its poison/toxin, disease, curse, intoxication, injury, environmental exposure or other underlying source. That cause may apply Poisoned again only through its own actual continuing or future trigger; do not invent an immediate reapplication just to negate the cure.

The source's abbreviated `bonus:1` or `bonus:3` is inactive here: complete effect prose promises advantage, not a numeric bonus. There is no damage resistance, immunity, general CON-save advantage, disease cure or intoxication emergency treatment. A target with no current Poisoned application can still receive the prospective save advantage.

## Healing and Local Treatment

At completion, attempt the printed dice and flat amount as ordinary magical, nonspell current-HP healing. Apply actual source blockers, modifiers, maximum and Critical ceilings, and eligible finite-healing callbacks. Positive HP recovery from dying follows the reviewed Core procedure; blocked healing does not invent stabilization. Dead creatures cannot be revived. These remedies do not automatically remove Wounds, Injuries, Burning, Poisoned, disease, Corruption or curses.

**Local Treatment:** After this dose's healing and all healing-triggered condition endpoints finish, choose at most one present local wound, burn, infection or Bleeding source appropriate to actual topical care and the remedy's ingredients. If the Bleeding source has an existing Medicine-based removal DC, the applier may immediately make one ordinary **WIS (Medicine)** check against that DC. The consumed remedy supplies dressing for this one attempt, with no additional healer's-kit charge. Actual Medicine proficiency applies once if possessed; none is newly granted or required. Use the source's check outcomes, or ordinary task success/failure with no invented extra critical benefit. Success ends only that eligible Bleeding source.

Do not make the extra Medicine check against a Bleeding record if this same dose's healing already resolved an explicit removal or treatment attempt for that same record, including an unsuccessful source save. An ended record cannot be selected. A different present eligible Bleeding record may be selected only if this dose's healing did not already resolve an explicit removal or treatment attempt for that different record. This gives no repeat attempt on one Blood Curse merely because the first save failed.

For another wound, burn or infection, the application may satisfy **one explicitly required topical dressing, cleaning, salve or comparable local step** in that source's existing treatment procedure. It does not waive or shorten any other required time, check, Supply, kit charge, medicine, surgery, rest or source-specific cure. If the source defines no topical-treatment interaction, the remedy has no additional automatic condition-removal effect. Treatment language alone cannot remove a Core Wound or its linked Injury; ordinary Wound care still takes its actual eight hours, medical kit, one Supply and Medicine check. Burning keeps its reviewed Action, immersion or save procedure unless its actual source permits this topical treatment.

The local-care component remains independent of actual HP gained; full HP or an HP-only blocker need not prevent a legal dressing. Broad suppression of the finished remedy's magic blocks its magical effects within that suppression's actual scope, without turning a spent dose into a reusable mundane treatment charge.

## Hazard bonuses

## Finished doses and common resolution

Each output unit is one magical nonspell **poison-effect** consumable. It requires no generic RP, RC, attunement, focus, concentration, class or proficiency to use. It creates no spell rank, spell access, Counterspell permission or Dissonance/Refrain event. All elemental varieties remain actual poison-effect applications; the printed damage type still controls damage defenses. Names and ingredient properties grant no additional effects. Only the current `mechanics.tag` supplies an operative recipe tag; preserve original tags and legacy text separately.

An actual legal exposure requires the appropriate delivery procedure. Resolve the printed **binary CON save** once: total meets DC succeeds, otherwise fails; natural 1/20 have no generic outcome shift. Success applies neither component. Failure attempts the exact printed initial damage and the printed condition independently. The initial damage is a separate save-based packet, not extra weapon damage; a critical weapon hit does not double its dice or make the poison save automatically fail. Apply the ordinary damage, temporary-HP, death and Wound procedure to each genuinely separate event without splitting or combining packets to manufacture thresholds.

Damage immunity and condition immunity operate independently. A zero-damage result does not prevent an otherwise legal condition; condition immunity does not erase damage. Explicit immunity covering the entire poison-effect/toxin application prevents both components and any new ongoing record, while the spent physical entitlement remains spent. No unnecessary die rolled for an application already prevented wholesale counts as a valid failed poison save.

Every actual source-specific anatomical restriction still applies. Creature type alone supplies no invented immunity or ineligibility. A creature must be a legal target of the actual delivery and effect. A Dead body receives no active creature-condition record. Inhaled delivery separately requires actual ambient-gas breathing; injury and contact use their own physical eligibility rules.

Every real exposure receives a unique `exposureId`, dose/deployment identity, recipe, applying DC, target, initial result and damage history. Replaying a record cannot spend another dose, roll another initial save or deal the initial damage again. Repeat saves **never repeat initial damage**. A suppressed initial effect is not banked for later unsuppression.

An ordinary condition has **ten future regular target-end markers**, representing one minute outside initiative. A singleton Flawed dose has five markers/30 seconds. Record the chosen virtual marker sequence once; initiative-order changes cannot shorten, extend or duplicate it. Extra turns and extra Actions never consume duration markers or add repeat saves.

- Application before the target's next regular turn begins: that upcoming regular turn's end is marker 1.
- Application during its already-in-progress regular turn: exclude that turn's end; marker 1 is the end of its next regular turn.
- Application after its regular turn ended: the next regular target-turn end is marker 1.

Outside initiative, preserve one step per complete six elapsed seconds and the already established virtual sequence across transitions. Do not reset the clock by entering/leaving initiative. All ordinary records receive the printed repeat CON save at each scheduled marker while their condition is still present. Success ends that record. The **final marker still gets its repeat CON save before expiry cleanup**; a failed final save does not extend the effect. If cure/expiry/another legal endpoint already ended the only condition, no later repeat save or initial-damage replay occurs.

Suppression and gained immunity can make a present record inactive without ending it. Its clocks and permitted ending saves continue. Applicable cures can remove a present suppressed record; active-condition hooks require actual unsuppressed eligibility. Initial immunity that prevented application creates no record to resume later. An ordinary elapsed rest does not automatically end a hostile poison unless its actual cure rule says so.

Keep these scopes separate:

| Effect | Scope |
|---|---|
| Poison-damage immunity/resistance | Only the actual poison-type damage packet. Other printed damage types retain their own defenses. |
| Core Poisoned immunity | Only a Poisoned component. |
| Named condition/profile immunity | The actual named applicable condition, not every poison symptom. |
| Explicit poison-effect/toxin immunity | Entire covered application: no initial damage, condition or repeat-save record. Physical expenditure still occurs. |
| Poison-save advantage | Initial and repeat CON saves of these poison effects regardless of damage type. It does not automatically cover Burning's separate DEX save. |
| Herbalism/other Poisoned-only cure | Present removable Poisoned records within its actual one/all scope. No Confused, Slowed, Weakened, Blinded, Frightened, Stunned or Burning removal by association. |
| Explicit end-one-poison-effect cure | One present removable poison application and its dependent ongoing symptoms. Independent sources and protected removal requirements remain. |

Removing an application's sole ongoing condition leaves only history; there is no hidden continuing toxin that later reapplies it without another real exposure. A lawful whole-application cure can select a present suppressed record. Damage already resolved is not undone.

A legal suppression effect covering magical nonspell poisons makes applicable established records inactive while their clocks and permitted ending saves continue. It supplies no later replay of initial damage. A finished poison suppressed at exposure spends its physical dose without banking future damage/conditions, unless the suppressing rule expressly provides another procedure. Never treat a rankless item as a rank-zero spell to create Counterspell or rank-limited dispel eligibility.

## Thief integration

**REVIEWED authored operational PLAYTEST equipment/acquisition scope.** These new procedures complete source item names and prices under the [equipment guide](EQUIPMENT_ACQUISITION_PLAYTEST.md). They do not claim to reproduce missing Player-book effect text. Use the complete [source tables](EQUIPMENT_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) for costs, weights and bundles.

Unless stated otherwise, using a consumable requires an Action, one available hand and access to the actual item. Spend one real unit. Drinking a potion or antitoxin, or feeding one to a willing or Incapacitated living creature within 5 feet, takes an Action. Inability to swallow blocks an oral dose. This gives no free way to dose an unwilling active creature. A potion, poison and healer's kit are not spells.

## Medicine and alchemy

| Item | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Basic Potion of Healing | Drink or feed to restore 2d4 + 2 ordinary HP, subject to actual healing blockers and caps. No Wound removal, resurrection, resource refill or stabilization of a Dead target. |
| Antitoxin | Drink or feed for advantage on saves against poison for one elapsed hour. It grants no immunity, automatic cure or advantage on unrelated CON saves. A new dose uses the later expiry without stacking advantage. |
| Healer's kit | A full 5-gp, 3-lb kit has ten consumable charges. Action and one charge automatically stabilize an adjacent living dying creature under the reviewed Core rule. Other medical procedures retain their own time, checks and charge costs. No universal HP healing. |
| Acid vial | Action: ranged improvised attack against one perceived creature or object within 20 feet, using DEX and PB only when actually eligible. Hit: 2d6 acid, with no ability damage. The vial is consumed hit or miss, with no splash or persistent acid pool. |
| Alchemist's fire | Use the same 20-foot Action attack as acid. A hit applies reviewed Burning at 1d4 fire, with no immediate damage. Its missing source DC uses the existing DC 10 fallback. Burning's family arbitration, regular-end pulses, saves and extinguishing procedures apply. Another flask does not create a second simultaneous winning fire-family pulse. |
| Holy water | Action: the same 20-foot ranged improvised attack, or a splash attack against one adjacent target. Hit: 2d6 radiant only if the target actually has Fiend or Undead type. The active Undead ancestry has that type. The flask is consumed even against an ineligible target. No inferred type from appearance or religious affiliation, and no extra exorcism. |
| Basic poison | Action: coat one piercing/slashing weapon or up to three compatible piercing/slashing ammunition units with one dose. For one elapsed minute, the first qualifying weapon hit, or first hit by each coated ammunition unit, forces DC 10 CON: failure takes 1d4 poison, success zero. That coating is then spent. No Poisoned condition. Coatings do not stack; expiry or washing ends them. |

| Mage Lich elite | Destroyed bound asset at 0; no usable corpse/resources | Same unique asset remains owned. Soulbound or actual completed LR can return it |
| Wizard standard undead | Destroyed at 0; consumed body never returns as new fuel | Ends on destruction, dismissal or owner's next completed LR, including Auto-Raised minions |
| Wizard elite | Supplied profile/cap only in this package | Binding/acquisition and return procedure are still missing; no create/bind/return API |
| Reflective Companion | Original creature's HP and life rules | Temporary control relation; no copied body, reset, new statistics or duplicate turn |
| Druid form | Same character's HP/life rules | Full forms and Buffer Reserve remain a separate open interface |

Companion healing restores legal normal HP only. It does not reset identity, duration, recharge, actions, source uses, effects or command budgets. Ranger's “heal normally” supplies no Hit Dice pool or automatic rest healing. The HP-only layer is specific to this reviewed companion chassis, not generic law for all animals/NPCs. Existing animal conditions, disease, poison, explicit injuries and timed effects survive bonding.

findings.finding: Detect Poison does not diagnose disease. Sacred Touch can detect a disease presence within its printed procedure without revealing origin or cure. Purify Drop expressly excludes pathogens; Purify Food and Drink removes eligible nonmagical contamination outside creatures but cannot cure an infected creature.
findings.authoringRequirement: Preserve separated batch, quantity, target, class/rank and detection limits. Record whether contamination is an object/food hazard or an established creature disease.

findings.finding: Contagion and Plague Wind remain blocked-pending-operational-review with no operational card. The inspected bestiary disease matches are pending source records: one Plaguehand attack name/flavor and four printed disease immunities.
findings.authoringRequirement: Route spell effects and creature combat implementation to their actual pending conferences. A new environmental disease must be clearly NEW scene authorship; these names do not authorize importing another game’s disease rules.

findings.finding: Herbalism topical care can supply one expressly required local step in an existing infection procedure; it cannot manufacture that procedure or waive its other costs. Antidotes remove eligible Poisoned, not disease.
findings.authoringRequirement: Print any useful topical-treatment step explicitly in the new disease profile, then preserve its remaining elapsed time, checks, medicine, kit and Supply costs. Full HP does not by itself invalidate the independent topical step.

findings.finding: Ranger bonding retains pre-existing disease/poison/conditions. Temporary form immunities, genuine disease immunity and nonmagical-only immunity require their own actual scopes; creature type alone does not erase disease.
findings.authoringRequirement: Work existing infection through bonding and form changes, using actual identity and clock records. Keep poison resistance and nonbreathing separate from disease protection.

findings.finding: The bounded source scan locates disease references and interfaces but does not establish a complete general environmental transmission/onset/progression/treatment framework.
findings.authoringRequirement: For the next NEW environmental disease candidate specify route and finite contamination source, susceptibility, initial exposure/cooldown, onset, actual symptoms, progression/repeat-save clock, failure/cure endpoints, reinfection and contact-spread permissions. Keep personal disease state separate from expedition Exposure pressure and from the unreviewed environment foundations proposal.

requiredFutureWorkedCases: Purify Food and Drink treats one eligible separated contaminated ration before ingestion; after infection the same spell cannot cure its consumer.
Purify Drop removes ordinary sediment from one legal drop but leaves pathogens; Detect Poison reports no disease diagnosis.
Mundane disease and magical disease independently target Purify Blood; only the magical branch invokes its actual treatment check and failed paid attempt.
Lay on Hands, Healing Touch and Stabilizing Injection face profiles with and without repeat saves; no generic instant cure or invented repeated save.
Petrified begins before onset, a scheduled event occurs while suspended, a legal cure removes the record, and unpetrifying does not resurrect it.
Carrion Rat King form ends with an older disease record; actual immunity scope and the ordinary body clock decide return of effects.
Ranger bonds an already-infected beast; disease state and source clock remain while ordinary companion HP/lifecycle rules still apply.
Topical balm heals zero at full HP but supplies exactly one explicitly permitted dressing step; other treatment costs remain.
A Poisoned-only antidote removes the symptom but retains independent disease; reapplication needs the disease’s actual future trigger.
Hush-Broker Contagion Touch source naming alone supplies neither an infection record nor a transmission event.
A source has ordinary disease plus poison damage; nonmagical disease immunity, Poisoned immunity and poison resistance are checked separately.
Rest across a disease onset/repeat-save deadline uses one elapsed timeline and does not duplicate expedition Exposure/Supply costs.
scopeLimits: Literal selection is bounded to the named files, not proof of absence across the archive.
Full preserved records include historical text and source status; no historical alternate or pending creature/spell is promoted.
Required future cases are specifications, not authored or executed test results.
